title: Streaming replication: primary, standby and replication slots

videos.script: When the promise is minutes, no restore fits. What fits is a server that is already restored. {{already}} A standby is a base backup that never finishes recovering. It receives the log as the primary writes it, and replays it, for as long as it runs. {{stream}} In this lesson you build one on your machine, on port 5434, with a role of its own and a slot on the primary. {{build}} You watch it stream, read from it, and see it refuse a write. {{watch}} Then you stop it, and keep the primary busy. The slot keeps every byte of log for a standby that is not coming back. {{slot}} That pile ends in a full disk, so you cap it. And the standby pays: it comes back, asks for its log, and is told the log is gone. {{lost}}
